description: Given the facts of an employment situation — claim types, protected class, employer, state — analyze how similar real cases in the corpus were decided. Returns the aggregate plaintiff (employee) win rate, settlement rate, typical damages range, the topics courts discussed most in opinions employees won vs. lost, and a few representative example cases. Counts are returned at three levels (nationwide, the federal courts of the state's region, and the state) with a detailed breakdown for one level: who won, award amounts, what happened at each stage, and topics. Relay which level a figure describes. A level with few opinions returns counts without a win rate. Each example says what happened and why it matched. Topic rows record what opinions discussed, not what courts found. Educational statistics from published opinions: never present a historical percentage as this person’s probability of winning. Not a prediction or legal advice. In structured stages: won and wonPct count opinions the worker won in whole or in part (wonPct leaves rulings sent back out of its base), and sentBack counts rulings sent back to a lower court. wentForward and wentForwardPct include rulings sent back to a lower court and are kept for compatibility.

claim_types.description: Claim types alleged, snake_case, e.g. ["retaliation","wrongful_termination","discrimination","harassment"]. The single highest-value signal.

employer_name.description: Employer / defendant name, e.g. "Union Pacific Railroad". Used for a fuzzy match.

law_ids.description: Related law ids, federal or state, e.g. ["title-vii","adea","ada","fmla","flsa","fl-fcra","ca-feha"].

level.description: Which level the detailed breakdown and examples describe: "national" (default), "circuit" (federal courts of the state's region), or "state". All three levels' counts are returned either way.

narrow_to_laws.description: Only count opinions that mention one of law_ids (a federal law or its state analogue). Default false: every opinion sharing the claim type, under any law.

state.description: Two-letter US state code the situation arose in, e.g. "FL", "CA".

name: find_similar_cases
title: Find how similar cases were decided
